summary: REGRESSION PASSED — all 11 backend cases verified after server.py was slimmed and prompts moved into /app/backend/prompts.py. Ran 14/14 pytest cases green in 23.7s against the public preview URL. The 8 pre-existing cases from test_iter7_ai_tools_v2.py (synonyms, antonyms, grammar happy + idempotent, idioms, vocab Tamil, vocab_full Telugu, chat, guest auth + /auth/me) still pass without any drift, and the 3 new cases added in test_iter8_refactor_regression.py (paraphrase → 3 variants stripped of numbering, translate 'Good morning' → 'Bonjour' (French Latin), OCR with a generated PNG of 'HELLO' → returns 'HELLO' or empty per the NO_TEXT_FOUND contract; plus OCR 400 on empty payload) all pass. critical_code_review_comments: prompts.py is cleanly extracted: TOOL_PROMPTS dict, MULTI_TOOLS set, CHAT_SYSTEM_MESSAGE, OCR_SYSTEM_MESSAGE, format_prompt(), text_matches_script(), vocab_payload_valid() — all behaviour-preserving. server.py imports the right symbols (lines 23-30) and re-binds them with leading underscores (_format_prompt, _vocab_payload_valid) which is fine.

MULTI_TOOLS is defined in prompts.py but server.py re-declares the same set inline at line 632 (multi_tools = {...}). Minor duplication — server.py could just `from prompts import MULTI_TOOLS` and use it directly. Not a bug; just dead-letter symbol.
server.py file is still ~970 lines — consider splitting auth, admin, subscription, AI, OCR/TTS into routers in a follow-up. Out of scope for this regression.
format_prompt() safely handles unknown tools by falling back to TOOL_PROMPTS['ask'] and swallows KeyError on .format() — robust against future template changes.
